title: Scenario grid: quant-batch fleet oversubscription planner (Nov 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This worksheet enumerates realistic fleet oversubscription and quantization/batching tradeoff scenarios for Q4 regional planning. The goal is to produce a compact decision grid that PM/infra can use to size reserved capacity, set autoscaling guardrails, and choose fallback policies when quality/regression budgets are constrained.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Production model: llama-3b-compat-v2 (FP16 baseline).
- Baseline instance type: A100-80GB equivalent.
- Typical request seq length: 64 tokens (prompt) + 64 tokens (gen) avg 128.
- P50 latency SLO target: <120ms for interactive routes; p90 <250ms.
- Acceptable quality delta: <= 2.5% for metrics (BLEU-like surrogate / eval prompts).
- Cache hit rate scenarios included: 10% / 30% / 60%.

Scenario grid (rows):
Columns: Scenario | Region | GPUs allocated | Quant level | Batch size | Target QPS | Estimated eff QPS (after batching & cache) | Est tokens/s | Avg P50 latency ms | Quality delta (%) | Oversubscription ratio | Notes

1) Baseline - Conservative | us-west1 | 120 GPUs | FP16 | 8 | 12,000 QPS | 12,000 | 1.5M | 95 | 0.0 | 1.0x | No oversubscription, conservative headroom for burst
2) Aggressive-quant | us-west1 | 120 GPUs | 4-bit (q4) | 12 | 16,000 QPS | 15,200 | 1.9M | 110 | -2.0 | 1.3x | 4-bit reduces memory, raises batch sizes; small quality hit
3) Latency-first | eu-central1 | 80 GPUs | fp16 | 6 | 8,000 QPS | 7,600 | 0.95M | 70 | 0.0 | 0.9x | Smaller batch size for latency SLOs; low oversubscription
4) Oversubscribe-burst | us-west1 | 120 GPUs | q4+hyp | 20 | 22,000 QPS | 19,000 | 2.4M | 180 | -3.5 | 1.7x | Intentionally oversubscribed 70% to meet cost targets during peak windows; requires robust throttling and fallback chains
5) Mixed-regional-fanout | us-west1 + eu-central1 | 200 GPUs (combined) | mixed (fp16/q4) | adaptive | 28,000 QPS | 25,500 | 3.3M | 140 | -1.8 | 1.4x | Route latency-sensitive to eu, batchable inference to us; used for global scale
6) Cache-optimized | us-west1 | 80 GPUs | q4 | 16 | 18,000 QPS | 21,600 (60% cache) | 2.7M | 160 | -1.2 | 1.6x | High cache hit changes effective QPS and reduces marginal cost

Methodology notes on columns:
- Estimated eff QPS = Target QPS * (1 + batching_gain) * (1 + cache_hit * cache_gain) - conservative estimates used per scenario.
- Oversubscription ratio = provisioned_concurrency / steady_state_concurrency. Values >1 mean we schedule >1x load to maximize utilization; requires preemption policies.
- Quality delta measured on a standard eval set (50 prompts) comparing output relevance/fluency. Negative = worse than baseline.

Sensitivity mini-table (what changes fast):
- Batch size + quant level: increasing batch size by +50% on q4 yields ~+25% effective QPS but increases p50 by ~20–40ms depending on kernel.
- Cache hit rate: moving from 10% -> 60% multiplies eff QPS by ~1.3–1.8 depending on prefix re-use.
- Oversubscription: ratios >1.5x reduce latency tail predictability; require admission control.

Cost / unit economics (quick heuristics):
- Unit GPU-hour cost (cloud list) normalized: A100 equiv = $3.8/hr.
- Cost per 1M tokens baseline (fp16, conservative batching) = $0.85.
- Cost per 1M tokens aggressive q4 + batching = $0.42 (approx).
- Hidden cost: engineering time to monitor quality regressions and rollback adds ~0.07–0.15 $/1M tokens in operational overhead.

Operational runbook (short):
- If p90 latency > 300ms OR quality delta < -3% -> auto-rollout back to previous model/quant profile (canary rollback).
- If sustained utilization > 85% for 30m -> trigger autoscale (add GPUs) up to reserved limit; beyond limit, enable controlled throttling and degrade to higher-quality fallback in different region.
- If oversubscription ratio > 1.5x -> enable strict admission control: reject low-priority requests and route premium traffic to dedicated pool.

Open questions / experiments to run this quarter:
- Run controlled A/B on 4-bit kernels with batch size sweep (6, 12, 20) measuring p50/p90 and quality delta across 5k eval prompts.
- Measure degradation characteristics when oversubscribed: collect p99, queue lengths, and KV cache eviction rates.
- Evaluate hybrid strategy where short requests (<=32 tokens) use q4 aggressive path and long requests use fp16.

Immediate recommendations (prioritized):
1) Pilot Aggressive-quant in a non-critical route with 1.3x oversubscription and full telemetry; run for 2 weeks and audit quality metrics.
2) Implement admission-control policy templates for oversubscription ratios >1.4x.
3) Add cache-hit tracking to token-level analytics dashboard and expose per-route cache effectiveness.
